title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Ĝ is a profinite group generated by two torsion elements ρ and σ with a central element -1. It is almost certainly the profinite completion of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, with σ^2 = -1 and ρ^3 = -1 (or ρ of order 6). Grothendieck works with the 'lacet' elements ε_0 = σρ and ε_1 = ρσ (up to sign), and with l_1 = ε_1^2, a parabolic (unipotent) generator, the loop around the cusp.

The group B_{ρ,σ}. It consists of pairs (u, μ), with u an automorphism of Ĝ and μ in Ẑ^*, such that:
- u sends ρ to a conjugate of ρ^μ;
- u sends σ to a conjugate of σ^μ;
- u sends the cusp loop to a conjugate of its μ-th power ('relation des lacets', (11)).
Since σ has order 4 and ρ has order 6 or 3, the powers reduce to signs: σ^μ = σ^{ε_2(μ)} and ρ^μ = ρ^{ε_3(μ)}.

This is the 'Grothendieck–Teichmüller type' group attached to the modular level M_{1,1}. Equivalently, it is the stratum of the Teichmüller tower given by the profinite modular group, i.e. B_3 modulo its centre.

The page continues the computation of the previous page.
- Write ξ = [u,ρ] = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = [u,σ] = u(σ)σ^{-1}.
- Using ε'_1 = ρσ^{-1} = -ε_1 and μ odd, the lacet condition becomes η^{-1}ξ = ε'_1^{2ν}, with ν = (μ-1)/2.
- Since ε'_1^{2ν} = ε_1^{2ν} = l_1^ν, the lacet relation takes the boxed form (16): ξ = η·l_1^ν, ν = (μ-1)/2.
- This is a direct analogue of the cusp/'lacet' relation in the genus-0 theory, written through the parabolic generator.

Lemma (17). If u(σ) is conjugate in Ĝ to σ^μ (= σ^{±1}), then u(-1) = -1. Proof: u(σ) = int(α)(σ') with σ' = σ^{±1}, so u(σ^2) = int(α)(σ'^2) = int(α)(-1) = -1.

Remark (17'). The conjugacy condition for σ is automatic from the parametrization (9), u(σ) = int(β)(σ^{ε_2(μ)}). For ρ, writing u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, the condition 'conjugate to ρ^μ' means α ≡ τ^{ν_3(μ)} modulo Ĝ, i.e. τ^{ν_3(μ)}α ∈ Ĝ. Here τ is an element of an ambient group that inverts ρ, and ν_3(μ) ∈ Z/2 is the exponent defining ε_3(μ).

Corollary (18). The map B_{ρ,σ} → Ĝ × Ĝ × Ẑ^*, (u,μ) ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], μ), is injective, since ρ and σ generate Ĝ. Its image Σ^eff_{ρ,σ} is the set of triples (ξ,η,μ) such that:
1. ξρ is conjugate to ρ^{ε_3(μ)};
2. ησ is conjugate to σ^{ε_2(μ)};
3. the lacet relation (16) holds (continued on the next page);
4. (ρ,σ) ↦ (ξρ, ησ) extends to an automorphism.

Next page. The inner automorphisms by a normal subgroup L_0 are divided out, giving Γ_{ρ,σ} = B_{ρ,σ}/L_0. This yields the extension 1 → L_0 → B → Γ → 1 and a character Γ → Ẑ^* with kernel Γ^+. This is the analogue of the construction of GT^ (or of its 'outer' version) at the M_{1,1} / SL2(Z) level. The purpose is to give an intrinsic description of a GT-like group acting on the profinite modular group, by solving the 'équation des lacets'.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. The lemma silently uses that μ ∈ Ẑ^* is odd; this is automatic, since units of Ẑ are units in Z_2.
The step 'conjugate to ρ^μ' ⇔ α ≡ τ^{ν_3(μ)} (mod Ĝ) is only sketched ('Dém. trivial').

That step requires knowing that the normalizer of ⟨ρ⟩ in the ambient group is generated by ⟨ρ⟩, the centre and τ. In the profinite completion this needs the fact that finite subgroups of the amalgam are conjugate into the factors and are self-normalizing up to the stated elements. That fact is true, but not stated.

ideas.what: Group B_{ρ,σ} of pairs (u,μ), with u an automorphism of the profinite modular group preserving the conjugacy classes of the torsion generators and of the cusp loop up to μ-th powers
ideas.modern_name: GT-type group for M_{1,1} / automorphisms of SL2(Z)^ or B_3^ with inertia condition; genus-one level of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990, via B_3 and the 2-cycle relation); Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Nakamura–Schneps (2000) for genus 1 and SL2-type relations
ideas.where_published: The program is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (§2, Teichmüller tower, 'modular' level 1); no explicit computation published

ideas.what: Lacet relation rewritten as ξ = η·l_1^{(μ-1)/2}, with l_1 the parabolic generator
ideas.modern_name: Cusp (parabolic) inertia relation, analogous to the defining relations of GT^ in terms of (λ,f)

ideas.what: Lemma: an automorphism preserving the conjugacy class of σ^{±1} fixes the central element -1
ideas.modern_name: Elementary fact on central involution σ^2 = -1

ideas.what: Injective parametrization B → Ĝ×Ĝ×Ẑ^* via commutators [u,ρ], [u,σ], with explicit description of the image
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of GT-type elements by (λ, f)-like data (cocycle description)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a self-contained 'GT for the modular group SL2(Z)^' using generators ρ, σ of orders 6 and 4 (rather than braid generators). He gives an explicit parametrization by triples (ξ,η,μ) with a boxed lacet relation ξ = η l_1^{(μ-1)/2}, and builds the extension 1 → L_0 → B → Γ → Ẑ^* on the next page. Comparing this Γ_{ρ,σ} with GT^, and with Nakamura–Schneps' genus-1 GT subgroup, does not appear to be done in his texts; a specialist could check whether his Γ^+ coincides with known groups.
missed.quote: (16) ξ = η l_1^ν où ν = (μ-1)/2 ... L'application (18) B_{ρ,σ} → Ĝ × Ĝ × Ẑ^* (u,μ) ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],μ) est injective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own, pre-Drinfeld, explicit treatment of the M_{1,1} level of the Teichmüller tower. This is relevant to the history of GT and to current work on elliptic GT groups (Enriquez) and genus-one profinite GT.

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit, unpublished Grothendieck computation of a GT-like group for the profinite modular group, with its own normal form for the lacet relation. It anticipates later work (Drinfeld, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps), but the mathematics on this page is fairly elementary and the concepts are now well known.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'η' ξ' is likely 'y^{-1}ξ' (i.e. η^{-1}ξ) = ε'_1^{2ν}; the crossed-out item after it is a deleted symbol.
Lemma statement: 'Soit u un automorphisme de Ĝ tel que u(σ) soit conjugué dans Ĝ à σ^μ (= σ ou σ^{-1})'.
Remark: 'u(ρ) = int(α)ρ est conjugué à ρ^μ, et u(σ) à σ^μ; cela est automatique pour σ, puisque u(σ) = int(β)(ε_2(μ)σ) = int(β)(σ^μ) (voir (9)), et pour ρ cela signifie que l'on a (17')'.
In condition 1°, 'ρ^{μ}' is probably the corrected reading of the target: ξρ is conjugate to ρ^μ = ρ^{ε_3(μ)}.
The '570' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number.
Next page: 'relation des Conti' should read 'relation des lacets (16)'.
